cohort: The study analyzed 127 cases of infants diagnosed with congenital anomalies at Basrah Maternity and Children Hospital.
finding: The most common congenital anomalies identified were musculoskeletal (33.9%), anencephaly (15.7%), and congenital hydrocephalus (10.2%), with factors such as gender, parental age, and consanguinity influencing anomaly patterns.
